production_connector.caller_id_comment: Stable pseudonymous ID for live tool cards and transport logs.
production_connector.caller_id_hash: sha256(raw identity) first 12 hex, prefixed caller_
production_connector.session_id_hash: sha256(raw session material) first 12 hex, prefixed session_

transport_snapshot.sources: clone-a/transport.jsonl plus all then-present transport.jsonl.archive/*.jsonl files
transport_snapshot.interpretation: When both fields are present in this deployment they are empirically redundant as continuity signals, not independent corroboration.

owl.boundary: This establishes stable connector association across those requests only.

supported: same exact external process when process_id/PID is identical
identity_claims.connection_id: transport plumbing; weaker than caller/session and not worker identity

evidence_order: upstream distributed trace ID (tracing-lineage continuity; not model-worker identity)

public_codex_context.rmcp_client_behavior: An initialized streamable-HTTP RmcpClient reuses its running service/session; on explicit session-expired 404 it builds a new transport and reinitializes.
public_codex_context.important_boundary: This describes MCP client-session lifetime, not model-worker lifetime.

upstream_trace_context.supported: Continuity of one upstream distributed tracing lineage across Stop -> go, plus overlapping upstream trace contexts after resume.
upstream_trace_context.not_supported: A Datadog trace ID is not established as a model-worker, inference-request, or app-turn identifier; distinct trace IDs do not prove distinct model workers.
